results.reason: Issue 1 calculates the Section 3.2 deadline as August 16, 2026 and says it has passed. It ties this to Schedule 3.12's statement that the Company only 'intends to deliver' the notice. It explains the agreement expires November 14, 2026, before the November 30 closing, and that the MIPA § 3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep would be false, exposing sellers to an indemnity claim. It hedges on whether a notice was sent, but the substance is identified.

Issue 2 treats the 100% sale as a Change of Control under §§ 1.3 and 14.2 with a termination right under § 14.3. It notes Velloran is missing from Schedule 3.6 and therefore from § 6.4 and § 7.1(d). It recommends adding the consent and starting the request immediately.

Issues 3 and 7 explain that the Side Letter § 1.1 adds NY and VA and controls under § 19.4. The non-compete therefore covers six states, including the 18-month tail, while exclusivity covers only four. It recommends narrowing the Side Letter Territory to match the four states.

The response mentions only the New York vs. Delaware governing-law difference and vague 'litigation complexity'. It does not address the exclusive New York County versus Wilmington forum clauses, the risk of split or inconsistent proceedings, or recommend conforming the Side Letter to Delaware.
